transcript.text: Thanks for joining. Pitch me Stripe — start with the basics.
Sure. Stripe is a payments company founded in 2010 by the Collison brothers, Patrick and John.
Good. And how would you frame its scale for an investor?
It's still private, and last I checked it was valued around 65 billion dollars after a down round.
You sure about that number? Walk me through it.
Yeah, roughly 65 billion. I think they also recently moved their headquarters to Dublin.
They acquired a metering company called Metronome to push into usage-based billing.

dimensions.label: Technical depth
dimensions.note: Solid on the fundamentals — founders, private status, the Metronome acquisition — but the valuation framing was a year stale.

dimensions.label: Communication
dimensions.note: Clear and direct; answered the question without rambling.

dimensions.label: Composure
dimensions.note: Doubled down on $65B when the MD pushed back instead of reconsidering — the moment that sinks the round.

dimensions.label: Structure
dimensions.note: Sensible arc: basics, then scale, then M&A — easy for the MD to follow.

debrief.composureNote: The MD gave you an opening — “you sure about that number?” — and you repeated $65B instead of reconsidering. Doubling down on a stale figure reads worse than the wrong number itself. The Dublin-HQ slip went unchallenged this round, but it's exactly the careless aside that ends a real pitch.
